markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (61%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert

Input is flagged, InSitu stays in the 90% set, and MUSK disagrees [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 61%, InSitu 33%, Normal 6%, Invasive 1% | Benign leads; InSitu plausible |
| Conformal set | {Benign, InSitu} at 90% | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.77 / OOD 1.0, flag on | Input suspect [F6] |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 Benign | Neighbors mostly disagree |

## Tissue evidence
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (regions 7, 10) · context · Above typical here; descriptive only · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Below typical here, lowering invasive association · Validated
- **Normal lobules** (region 0) · ↓ invasive · Scored below typical; spot check failed, 0/20 · Unreliable
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Slightly above typical; relevant to InSitu versus Benign · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Deletion CI excludes 0 (+0.54 logit, 0.47 to 0.60); faithful to the invasive logit.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (+0.002); not shown to reflect classifier use. Normal lobules (0/20) unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Blur and extreme OOD score distort probabilities; the second model already disagrees.
- Neighbors include 2 Invasive and 2 InSitu; similarity alone cannot rule out invasion.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 5**: duct-confined atypia and highest per-region invasive probability (76%).
2. **Region 3**: look for infiltrating stroma; top region of this validated concept.
3. **Region 0**: confirm whether normal lobules or tubules are truly present.
